title: Spiritual Disciplines
definition: Spiritual Disciplines are Scripture-shaped practices that help believers seek God, receive grace, and grow in Christlikeness.
summary: Spiritual Disciplines are Scripture-shaped practices that help believers seek God, receive grace, and grow in Christlikeness.
christFocus: Jesus practiced prayer, Scripture, solitude, worship, and obedience, and He teaches His people to walk with God in dependent rhythms.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Spiritual disciplines do not earn salvation. They are means by which believers place themselves before God to receive His Word, seek His presence, and grow in grace.

Practices such as prayer, Scripture reading, fasting, worship, fellowship, service, and confession help train the heart toward Christ.

The disciplines are fruitful when empowered by the Spirit and rooted in the Gospel. Without grace, they become performance; with grace, they become pathways of communion.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers avoid disciplines because they have known legalism. Others neglect them and wonder why they feel spiritually weak. This doctrine restores disciplines as grace-shaped practices, not religious scorekeeping.

Steady rhythms can especially help people rebuilding life in recovery or hardship.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Choose one simple discipline and practice it with Gospel freedom. Begin small, stay consistent, and ask the Holy Spirit to use that rhythm to draw you nearer to Christ.
